messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: p99 tail latency > 10s for /v1/stream (customer: BlueOak Labs, single-tenant VPC). Alert link: <https://redwood/alert/1700000000>

sam: picking this up — seeing a spike starting ~1700000000, p95 ~450ms but p99 ~12s and streaming stalls (clients report partial payloads).

meera: I'm oncall. Is BlueOak on Dedicated or Private?

sam: Private VPC (vpc-blueoak-us-east-1), reserved capacity, single-tenant pool id: pool-bo-7. High concurrency reported from their batch workers.

sam: quick snapshot from metrics:
```
metric: request.count{customer=blueoak} = +3x baseline over last 5m
metric: latency.p95 = 0.45s
metric: latency.p99 = 12.3s
streaming: aborts = 37 in last 10m
kvcache: evictions/sec = 420
```

meera: interesting — evictions/sec is huge. Could be KV cache fragmentation. Any unusual prompt patterns?

sam: BlueOak provided sample requests — many prompts include long unicode emoji sequences and multi-line transcript fragments. Example: "User: 🧾📜🚨🚨🚨 ... (repeated)" — lots of multibyte graphemes and repeated tokens.

meera: that can blow up prefix matching and cause a lot of unique cache keys, eviction thrash under high concurrency. Hypothesis: KV cache churn + batching behavior + streaming frontends trying to hold open sessions -> tail stalls.

meera: @eng-runtime-bot can you pull the pool kernel logs and attach last 30s of sched traces for pool-bo-7?

eng-runtime-bot: Attached logs for pool-bo-7 (tail -n 200 /var/log/serving/pool-bo-7/kernel.log). Key excerpts:
```
2024-05-14T12:00:10Z [runtime] kv_cache: set key=prefix:U:0x7f9.. size=512
2024-05-14T12:00:11Z [runtime] kv_cache: evict key=prefix:U:0x1b2.. reason=LRU
2024-05-14T12:00:16Z [runtime] batcher: flush start size=1
2024-05-14T12:00:16Z [runtime] stream: write error: EPIPE (client aborted)
2024-05-14T12:00:20Z [runtime] kv_cache: evictions/sec=430
```

lucy: adding context — BlueOak's client concurrency went from 8 -> 48 workers at 11:59. They pushed a job early.

meera: mitigation plan (short term, seconds->minutes):
- throttle BlueOak to 20rps on the ingress gateway (temporary).
- flip feature flag: prefix_dedup=true for pool-bo-7 to collapse near-identical long prefix keys.
- route heavy streaming sessions to model-variant: gpt-eco-small (lower mem KV pressure) for this customer until stable.

sam: I'll run the commands.

sam: throttling via gateway:
```
# api gateway config
redwoodctl gateway update-rate --customer blueoak --rate 20
```

sam: prefix dedup flag flip (canary) for pool-bo-7:
```
redwoodctl feature-flag set prefix_dedup=true --pool pool-bo-7 --canary 10%
```

sam: route step (immediate fallback):
```
redwoodctl route set --customer blueoak --pool pool-bo-7 --model gpt-eco-small --fallback true
```

meera: +1 to those. Also increase kv_cache size for pool-bo-7 to reduce thrash (medium-term, minutes):
```
redwoodctl pool update --id pool-bo-7 --kv-cache-mb 1536
```

jonah: I'll watch the dashboard and logs. If p99 drops under 2s and streaming abort rate drops, we can slowly relax throttling.

(90s later)

sam: throttle applied, prefix_dedup canary at 10% and route fallback to gpt-eco-small active. kv_cache increased to 1536MB (scaling rolling restart for pool-bo-7).

sam: immediate effect: p99 dropped from 12.3s -> 1.9s, streaming aborts from 37 -> 4 in 10m window. Evictions/sec down to ~60.

meera: good. Keep the throttles in place until we confirm a stable 30m window. Notify BlueOak SRE and product contact.

sam: pinged BlueOak SRE (via private channel) — they confirm they accidentally started an extra job. They can reschedule.

lucy: action items for post-incident:
- eng-runtime: investigate prefix hash distribution for multibyte graphemes (owner: eng-runtime).
- platform: consider default prefix_dedup for private pools handling untrusted prompts (owner: meera).
- devex: add a runbook step for customer bulk jobs and recommended rate guidance (owner: sam).
- support: reach out to BlueOak with explanation + short term config changes (owner: lucy).

meera: handoff: I'm staying on until 1700000600. After that, jonah will be primary. Jonah — check the 30m SLO window and the rollout logs for the canary.

jonah: copy. I'll take it at 1700000600. I'll also ask eng-runtime for a flame profile during the next induced load to find hotspots.

eng-runtime-bot: noted. Scheduling kernel profile capture for pool-bo-7 during expected next load window.

meera: postmortem: yes. Sev: P2 (customer-facing but mitigated without data loss). Tentative authors: meera (lead), sam (mitigations), eng-runtime (root cause).

sam: leaving a short incident summary in #incidents-status for customers and execs. Will attach metrics + timeline.

meera: thanks team. Monitoring continues. If any regressions, we escalate to eng-runtime pager. :memo:

jonah: oncall handoff acknowledged.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket: INC-2024-BO-1700000000
